mainTopic: When a husband can take back a גט, and how agents for delivering and receiving a גט work
overview: The amud opens by asking whether, for רבי נתן, a husband who says "הֵילָךְ" (Here you are) to an agent is like one who says "זְכֵי" (Acquire), so that he cannot take the גט back. Two proofs from the משנה are pushed off, but a ברייתא proves that "הֵילָךְ" is like "זְכֵי". Next, רב rules that when the wife sends an agent to receive the גט and the husband tells him "deliver it," the agent counts as both of theirs, so she needs חליצה. The גמרא explains this by contrasting money doubts, which are ruled leniently, with איסור doubts, which are ruled strictly. רב and רבי חנינא then argue whether a woman can appoint an agent to receive her גט from her husband's agent. A real case of a woman kneading dough ends in doubt, so she needs a גט while her husband lives, or חליצה after he dies. Then רב, רבה and רב נחמן argue about when witnesses sent to write a גט have finished their mission. The amud ends with phrases that make a receiving agent and the start of a new משנה about the witnesses needed for him.

steps.title: Trying to read the משנה's case as 'Here you are' following רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the case just quoted from the משנה is about a husband who said הֵילָךְ, and that it follows רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this case about a husband who said 'Here you are,' and doesn't it follow רבי נתן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to use the case it just quoted to answer its question. It suggests the husband there said "הֵילָךְ" and that the ruling follows רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case really is "הֵילָךְ" and it follows רבי נתן, then the ruling would tell us how רבי נתן treats "הֵילָךְ". That would settle the open question.

keyTerms.meaning: "Isn't it…?" A way of suggesting how to read a source as a proof
"Here you are": the husband hands over the גט with these words

phrases.english: What, is it not where he said "Here you are"
and it follows רבי נתן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a proof from the source quoted just before this section
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case from the משנה quoted just before

steps.title: No, the case is 'Deliver,' following רבי
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The case could be about הוֹלֵךְ, and it could follow רבי instead of רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is about a husband who said 'Deliver,' and it follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. It reads the case a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that even "הוֹלֵךְ" works like "זְכֵי" and cannot be taken back. So the case can be about "הוֹלֵךְ" following רבי, and it teaches us nothing about רבי נתן's view of "הֵילָךְ".

keyTerms.meaning: "No": rejects the proposed reading
"Deliver": the husband sends the agent to bring the גט

phrases.english: No; it is where he said "Deliver"
and it follows רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case can just as easily be about הוֹלֵךְ following רבי

steps.title: A new proof from the משנה: 'I do not want you to receive for her'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the husband told the woman's agent "I do not want you to receive it for her, just deliver it," he can take it back. The גמרא reads this closely: only because he said "I do not want" can he take it back. Without those words, he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if the husband said, 'I do not want you to receive it for her, but deliver and give it to her,' he can take it back if he wants. The reason is that he said 'I do not want.' If he did not say that, he could not take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another line of the משנה and reads it closely. It is setting up a second attempt to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "I do not want" cancel the agent's role as the woman's receiving agent. That is why the husband can take the גט back. So when the husband does not say those words, he cannot take it back. The גמרא will now ask what words he did use in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: "Therefore": the משנה draws a result from what it said before
"I do not want"
"If he wants to take it back"
"The reason is… but otherwise…": learning the opposite case from the reason given

phrases.english: Come and hear: Therefore,
if the husband said to him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the agent the wife sent to receive the גט for her.

phrases.english: "I do not want you to receive it for her,
rather, deliver and give it to her,"
if he wants to take it back, he can take it back.
The reason is that he said "I do not want";
but if he did not say "I do not want,"
if he wants to take it back, he cannot take it back;

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לְפִיכָךְ, אִם אָמַר לוֹ הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, brings a new source
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of "I do not want" and what it implies

steps.title: Reading the implied case as 'Here you are' following רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the implied case (no 'I do not want,' and he cannot take it back) is about הֵילָךְ following רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that case about 'Here you are,' following רבי נתן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the same kind of suggestion as in step 1, now using the implied case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is "הֵילָךְ" and he cannot take it back according to רבי נתן, then רבי נתן treats "הֵילָךְ" like "זְכֵי".

phrases.english: What, is it not where he said "Here you are"
and it follows רבי נתן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the inference in step 3
steps.raayaObject: That הֵילָךְ is like זְכֵי for רבי נתן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied case of the משנה

steps.title: Again, the case could be 'Deliver' following רבי
steps.stepSummary: The second proof is pushed off in the same way as the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is about 'Deliver,' and it follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof with the same answer it gave before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי, even "הוֹלֵךְ" cannot be taken back. So the implied case may be "הוֹלֵךְ" and tells us nothing about רבי נתן.

phrases.english: No; it is where he said "Deliver"
and it follows רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 4
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case can be הוֹלֵךְ following רבי

steps.title: A בריתא: 'Deliver' can be taken back, 'Here you are' cannot
steps.stepSummary: A בריתא rules that with הוֹלֵךְ the husband can take the גט back, but with הֵילָךְ he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'Deliver this גט to my wife': he can take it back if he wants. 'Here you are, this גט is for my wife': he cannot take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a בריתא that rules on both wordings side by side. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the בריתא names both "הוֹלֵךְ" and "הֵילָךְ" and rules differently on them, there is no room to say it is all "הוֹלֵךְ".

keyTerms.meaning: Document of divorce
"To my wife"

phrases.english: Come and hear: "Deliver this גט to my wife"
if he wants to take it back, he can take it back.
"Here you are, this גט is for my wife"
if he wants to take it back, he cannot take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two failed proofs, brings a clearer source
steps.raayaObject: That הֵילָךְ is like זְכֵי for רבי נתן

steps.title: The בריתא must be רבי נתן, so 'Here you are' is like 'Acquire'
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי נתן holds that הוֹלֵךְ can be taken back, so the בריתא follows him. Since it says הֵילָךְ cannot be taken back, הֵילָךְ is like זְכֵי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who holds that with 'Deliver' he can take it back? רבי נתן. And this same source says that with 'Here you are' he cannot. Learn from here that 'Here you are' is like 'Acquire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out whose opinion the בריתא follows and draws the answer to its question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי would not let the husband take back "הוֹלֵךְ". So a source that does allow it must be רבי נתן. That same source makes "הֵילָךְ" final, so for רבי נתן, "הֵילָךְ" works like "זְכֵי".

keyTerms.meaning: "Whom have you heard say…?": figuring out which תנא a source follows
"Acquire": the agent acquires the גט for the wife right away
"Is like…": is treated the same as

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even רבי נתן agrees that handing the גט over with "הֵילָךְ" makes it final, the same as "זְכֵי".

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says
that with "Deliver," if he wants to take it back, he can take it back
It is רבי נתן;
and he says that with "Here you are"
if he wants to take it back, he cannot take it back;
learn from it: "Here you are" is like "Acquire";

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the בריתא of step 6 to make the proof
steps.raayaObject: הֵילָךְ is like זְכֵי for רבי נתן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The בריתא, shown to follow רבי נתן

steps.title: Conclusion: the proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that the proof works and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one pushes back on the בריתא's proof, so the answer stands: for רבי נתן, "הֵילָךְ" is like "זְכֵי".

keyTerms.meaning: "Learn from it": said a second time, it means the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי נתן: "הוֹלֵךְ" can be taken back, but "הֵילָךְ" cannot, because it is like "זְכֵי". רבי: even "הוֹלֵךְ" cannot be taken back. That is why the proofs from the משנה failed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up הוֹלֵךְ ("Deliver") and הֵילָךְ ("Here you are"). They look alike, but the whole סוגיא depends on the difference between them.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי נתן, הֵילָךְ is treated like זְכֵי, so the husband cannot take the גט back.

steps.title: רב: the agent becomes both the husband's and the wife's agent
steps.stepSummary: When the wife's receiving agent is told by the husband 'deliver it to her,' רב rules the agent is both of theirs, so she must do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a woman told her agent, 'Receive my גט for me.' The agent told the husband, 'Your wife said: receive my גט for me.' The husband answered, 'Deliver it and give it to her.' רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא, who said in the name of רב: the agent becomes both the husband's agent and the wife's agent, so she does חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case: the wife appointed an agent to receive her גט, but the husband treated him as an agent to deliver it. רב rules that the agent counts as both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A receiving agent for the wife makes the divorce take effect right away, while a delivery agent for the husband only makes it take effect when the גט reaches her. Because the husband's words 'הוֹלֵךְ וְתֵן לָהּ' leave us unsure which kind of agent he is, רב treats him as both and is strict both ways. If the husband dies childless before the גט reaches her, she needs חליצה, since maybe she was still married.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Receive my גט for me.' This is the wife appointing an agent to receive the גט on her behalf.
'Deliver and give it to her.' This is the husband's wording for a delivery agent.
His agent and her agent, meaning the agent counts as both.
She performs חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from her brother-in-law.

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying she is definitely still married. He is unsure, so she does חליצה (in case she is still married) but cannot do יבום (in case she was already divorced).

phrases.english: It was stated: [she said] "Receive my bill of divorce for me,"
and [the agent said to the husband] "Your wife said: Receive my bill of divorce for me,"
and he [the husband] says: "Deliver and give it to her"

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
He becomes his agent and her agent
and she performs חליצה.
phrases.notes: This is for the case where the husband dies childless before the גט reaches her. Since we're unsure whether she was divorced, she gets חליצה and not יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case after the גמרא finished proving that הֵילָךְ is like זְכֵי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An agent appointed by the wife to receive, whom the husband tells 'deliver,' is the agent of both; if the husband dies before delivery, she does חליצה.

steps.title: Was רב really unsure? He treated 'deliver' like 'acquire' in a money case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's doubt from his own ruling that someone sending a debt payment with 'deliver' cannot take it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רב was unsure whether 'deliver' is like 'acquire' or not? But it was taught: if someone said, 'Deliver a מָנֶה to so-and-so, since I owe it to him,' רב said the sender is still responsible for it, and if he wants to take it back, he cannot!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on רב. His ruling in the גט case shows he was unsure about הוֹלֵךְ, but in a debt case he seemed sure that הוֹלֵךְ works like זְכֵי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the debt case רב said the sender cannot take the money back. That sounds like the creditor already acquired it the moment it was handed to the agent, which is exactly how זְכֵי works. If so, why was רב unsure in the גט case?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is this to say...?' An opening that introduces a challenging inference.
He is in doubt about it.
A sum of money (one hundred זוז).
He bears responsibility for it, meaning he must pay if it gets lost.
He cannot take it back.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rav is uncertain
whether "deliver" is like "acquire,"
or whether it is not like "acquire"?!
But wasn't it stated:
"Deliver a מָנֶה to so-and-so
since I owe it to him,"
Rav said: he bears responsibility for it,
and if he comes to retract, he cannot retract!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the doubt implied in רב's ruling in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The doubt about הוֹלֵךְ that רב's ruling implies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the debt case רב ruled the sender cannot retract, which suggests he holds that הוֹלֵךְ is like זְכֵי. That contradicts his doubt in the גט case.

steps.title: Money doubts are handled leniently, איסור doubts strictly
steps.stepSummary: רב is unsure in both cases. In the money case the doubt gives a lenient result, and in the גט case the doubt gives a strict result.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a doubt about money, so we go easy. Here, it is a doubt about an איסור, so we are strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב really is unsure in both cases. The rulings only look different because money doubts and איסור doubts follow different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a money doubt we do not take money away on a doubt. So the sender stays responsible, because maybe the creditor never acquired it. He also cannot take it back, because maybe it already belongs to the creditor. Both rulings fit a doubt, so the debt case does not prove that הוֹלֵךְ is like זְכֵי. In a doubt about an איסור, like whether a woman is married, we are strict, which is why she does חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt about money is ruled leniently, so we don't take money away on a doubt.
A doubt about a prohibition is ruled strictly.
There / here. Used to contrast the two cases.

steps.whatToRemember: רב is consistently unsure whether הוֹלֵךְ is like זְכֵי. The outcome changes only because money doubts are ruled leniently and איסור doubts strictly.

phrases.english: There, it is a monetary doubt, ruled leniently;
phrases.notes: 'There' is the debt case. Both of רב's rulings there come from not taking money from anyone when we're unsure.

phrases.english: here, it is a doubt about a prohibition, ruled stringently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the type of doubt (money vs. איסור).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's debt ruling shows he is sure that הוֹלֵךְ is like זְכֵי.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב is unsure in both cases. The debt ruling reflects leniency in a money doubt, and the גט ruling reflects strictness in an איסור doubt.

steps.title: Can a woman send an agent to receive her גט from her husband's agent?
steps.stepSummary: רב says a woman cannot appoint an agent to receive her גט from her husband's agent. רבי חנינא says she can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: a woman cannot appoint an agent to receive her גט from the hand of her husband's agent. רבי חנינא said: a woman can appoint an agent to receive her גט from the hand of her husband's agent.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens with a disagreement between רב and רבי חנינא. Here the husband's agent already has the גט, and the question is whether the wife's agent can receive it from him. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is no longer about one agent serving both sides. It is about two separate agents: the husband's delivery agent and the wife's receiving agent. רב says the wife's agent cannot receive from the husband's agent, and רבי חנינא says he can. No reasons are given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Appoints an agent.
To receive her גט on her behalf.
From the hand of her husband's agent.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: אֵין הָאִשָּׁה עוֹשָׂה שָׁלִיחַ
phrases.english: Rav said: A woman cannot appoint an agent
to receive her bill of divorce for her
from the hand of her husband's agent.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: אִשָּׁה עוֹשָׂה שָׁלִיחַ
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina said: A woman can appoint an agent
to receive her bill of divorce for her
from the hand of her husband's agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֵין הָאִשָּׁה עוֹשָׂה שָׁלִיחַ לְקַבֵּל לָהּ גִּיטָּהּ מִיַּד שְׁלִיחַ בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of רב's doubt was resolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a woman cannot appoint an agent to receive her גט from her husband's agent. רבי חנינא: she can.

steps.title: What is רב's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב rules that a woman cannot appoint an agent to receive her גט from her husband's agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רב's ruling from step 12. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a woman can appoint an agent to receive her גט. So רב's rule that she cannot do this when the husband's agent is delivering it needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Agent, messenger

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rav?
phrases.notes: This refers back to רב's rule that she can't appoint her own agent to take the גט from the husband's agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רב's ruling in step 12.

steps.title: First reason: disrespect to the husband
steps.stepSummary: One possible reason is that refusing to take the גט directly from the husband's agent looks like disrespect to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: it is because of disrespect to the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. The problem is that she seems to be insulting her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband sent his own agent to her. If she says 'I won't take it from your agent, give it to mine,' it looks like a snub. רב does not allow this.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (it introduces one of several possible answers)
Disrespect, contempt

phrases.english: If you wish, say: because of disrespect to the husband;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It would be disrespectful to the husband.

steps.title: Second reason: confusion with a courtyard that becomes hers later
steps.stepSummary: Another possible reason is a precaution, so that people do not confuse this case with a courtyard that becomes hers only after the גט was placed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: it is because of her courtyard that comes to her afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different reason for רב's rule. It is a safeguard against a mistake people might make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a husband puts a גט in a courtyard and she buys that courtyard only later, the divorce does not work. Here she appoints her agent only after the husband's agent already holds the גט, which looks similar. Allowing it might lead people to think the later-courtyard case works too.

keyTerms.meaning: Her courtyard (a woman's property can receive a גט for her)
Afterward, later on

steps.confusionAlert: This second reason does not say the agent is literally a courtyard. It is a safeguard: the two cases look alike, so people could mix them up.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
because of her courtyard that comes to her afterward.
phrases.notes: He means a courtyard she gets only after the גט was already put there, where the divorce doesn't take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִשּׁוּם חֲצֵרָהּ הַבָּא לְאַחַר מִיכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A safeguard so that people do not confuse this with a courtyard acquired after the גט was placed in it.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical case where the two reasons would give different rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two reasons ever lead to different results. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

steps.deeperAnalysis: When the גמרא gives two reasons, it often checks where they actually split. That shows the two reasons are not just two ways of saying the same thing.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in steps 14 and 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: she appointed her agent first
steps.stepSummary: The two reasons differ where she appointed her receiving agent before the husband appointed his delivery agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them where she went first and appointed an agent from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the case where the two reasons split. That case is where she appointed her agent before her husband appointed his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her agent was appointed first, it no longer looks like the courtyard she got later, so the second reason does not apply. But the disrespect to the husband may still be there, so under the first reason it is still not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
She went first, she preceded
From the start, originally

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for רב's rule. The first is disrespect to the husband. The second is a safeguard against confusion with a courtyard she got later. They differ only when she appointed her agent first.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them where she went first,
and appointed an agent from the start.
phrases.notes: 'From the start' means before the husband handed the גט to his own agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ when she appointed her agent before the husband appointed his. The courtyard concern is gone, but the disrespect concern may remain.

steps.title: A story: the woman kneading dough
steps.stepSummary: A husband's agent brought a גט to the wife while she was kneading. She told him, 'Let it be in your hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man sent a גט to his wife. The agent went and found her sitting and kneading. He said to her, 'Here is your גט.' She said to him, 'Let it be in your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that connects to the argument between רב and רבי חנינא. This story sets up רב נחמן's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her hands were full of dough, so she asked the husband's agent to hold the גט. That makes him her agent to receive it. This is just the kind of case that רב and רבי חנינא argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Sent
Kneading (dough)
Here you are, take it
Let it be in your hand

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּשַׁדַּר לַהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ,
phrases.english: There was a certain man who sent a bill of divorce to his wife.
The agent went and found her
while she was sitting and kneading.
He said to her: 'Here is your bill of divorce.'
She said to him: 'Let it be in your hand.'
phrases.notes: She is asking him to hold it for her, which makes him her agent to receive it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּשַׁדַּר לַהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests the argument between רב and רבי חנינא in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case facts: the wife made the husband's agent her agent to receive the גט.

steps.title: רב נחמן ties the case to רבי חנינא's view
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that if the view of רבי חנינא is accepted, he would act on this case and treat the divorce as valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: If the view of רבי חנינא is accepted, I would act on this case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his response to the story. He makes his ruling depend on whether we follow רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי חנינא, she may appoint an agent to receive the גט from the husband's agent, so this divorce would work. Under רב, it would not. רב נחמן speaks only conditionally: 'if' רבי חנינא's view holds.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is so
I would act on it (rule on it in practice)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the argument between רב and רבי חנינא decides real cases. Whether this woman is divorced depends on whose view we follow.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
If the view of Rabbi Ḥanina is accepted,
phrases.notes: רבי חנינא is the one from step 12 who allows her to appoint an agent to receive from the husband's agent.

phrases.english: I would act on this case.
phrases.notes: He means he would rule that the divorce takes effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אִם אִיתָא לִדְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling on the story told in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If we follow רבי חנינא, this divorce would be valid in practice.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that even according to רבי חנינא, the divorce should not work, because the husband's agency was never completed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Even if the הלכה follows רבי חנינא, would you act on it in this case? The agency never got back to the husband!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back against רב נחמן's statement from the previous step. He says this case does not work even according to רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's שליח never actually handed the גט to the woman, so his job for the husband was not finished. When she made him her own agent first, she cut off the husband's agency, so the divorce cannot take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so (if we accept this view)
Would you act on it in practice?
Agency, the job of acting for someone else
Returned to the husband (the agency was completed for him)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not rejecting רבי חנינא. He is saying that even if you accept רבי חנינא, this specific case still fails.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
And if the view of Rabbi Chanina is accepted,
would you act on it in practice?!

phrases.aramaic: הָא לֹא חָזְרָה שְׁלִיחוּת אֵצֶל הַבַּעַל!
phrases.english: But the agency did not return to the husband!
phrases.notes: He means the agent never finished the job the husband gave him, since he never actually handed her the גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְאִם אִיתָא לִדְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's practical ruling in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that he would validate the divorce under רבי חנינא's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even under רבי חנינא, the husband's agency was cut off before it was completed, so the divorce fails.

steps.title: רבי אמי rules the divorce does not work
steps.stepSummary: The question is sent to רבי אמי, who agrees with רבא that the husband's agency was not completed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent the question to רבי אמי. He sent back: The agency did not return to the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The case is sent to a bigger authority, רבי אמי, to decide. He rules like רבא: the divorce does not take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי repeats רבא's exact words. This shows he accepts the reasoning that her appointing the agent cancelled the husband's agency before it was done.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent it (the question) before him
He sent back to them

phrases.english: They sent it before Rabbi Ami,
phrases.notes: "They" is רב נחמן and רבא, sending the question to the sages of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he sent back to them:
The agency did not return to the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's challenge with a ruling from רבי אמי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband's agency was not completed, so the divorce does not take effect.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא asks for time to think
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא does not rule right away; he says he will think the matter over.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said: We will think about the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage, רבי חייא בר אבא, holds back from deciding. This sets up the next step, where they ask him again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי אמי, he is not sure. His hesitation shows the case is not simple, which prepares for the final uncertain answer.

keyTerms.meaning: We will think the matter over

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said:
We will think about the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: נִתְיַישֵּׁב בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, undecided response to the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet; the matter needs more thought.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא admits he is also unsure
steps.stepSummary: When asked again, רבי חייא בר אבא says the question is just as uncertain to him as it is to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent it again to רבי חייא בר אבא. He said: Are they going to keep sending this? Just as it is uncertain for them, it is uncertain for us too.
steps.whatsHappening: The question comes back to רבי חייא בר אבא. He admits he cannot resolve it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His earlier 'let us think' ends in a clear admission of doubt. Because no one can settle it, the case stays a ספק, which leads directly into the גמרא's conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Again
They keep on sending it
It is uncertain to them

phrases.aramaic: הֲדוּר שַׁלְחוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: They sent it again before Rabbi Chiya bar Abba,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: כֹּל הָנֵי שָׁלְחוּ לַהּ וְאָזְלִי?
phrases.english: he said: All these times they keep sending it?
Just as it is uncertain to them,
so too it is uncertain to us.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדוּר שַׁלְחוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי חייא בר אבא's response from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question is unresolved; it remains a doubt.

steps.title: Because of the doubt, she needs חליצה
steps.stepSummary: Since it is a doubt about a forbidden relationship, we are strict, and the woman must do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a matter of forbidden relations, and in a doubtful matter of forbidden relations, she does חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical bottom line for this uncertain case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether she is still married is a question of ערוה, so we go strict both ways. If her husband dies without children, she cannot remarry without חליצה in case the divorce failed, and the brother cannot do יבום in case the divorce worked.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter involving forbidden relationships
She does חליצה (the release ceremony with the husband's brother)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא and רבי אמי say the husband's agency was cut off, רבי חייא בר אבא stays in doubt, and the final practical answer is to be strict: the woman needs חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the standard rule that when a doubt touches on forbidden relationships, we take the strict path on every side.

phrases.english: It is a matter of forbidden relations,
and in a matter of forbidden relations, she does chalitza.
phrases.notes: This matters if her husband later dies with no children; she needs חליצה and cannot have יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי דָּבָר שֶׁבָּעֶרְוָה, וְדָבָר שֶׁבָּעֶרְוָה חוֹלֶצֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the unresolved doubt from step 23 into a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case remains a doubt; since it involves ערוה, we are strict and she needs חליצה.

steps.title: A real case: both a גט and חליצה required
steps.stepSummary: In an actual case, רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא required the woman to get both a גט and חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a real case, and רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא required the woman to receive a גט and also חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how the doubtful divorce from the earlier discussion was handled in a real case. The ruling requires two things: a גט and חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the divorce is a doubt, so we are strict. Because she may still be married, she needs a proper new גט, or חליצה if her husband dies childless. Because she may already be divorced, יבום is not allowed, which is why it must be חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A real-life case that came before the rabbis
He required her (to do something)
The ceremony that releases a widow from marrying her husband's brother

phrases.english: There was an incident,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַצְרְכַהּ רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא
phrases.english: and Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta required her
a bill of divorce and chalitza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the strict ruling of step 24 was applied in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a doubtful divorce like this one, the woman needs both a גט and חליצה.

steps.title: How can both be needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how she can need both a גט and חליצה at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that two remedies are needed. A גט and חליצה seem to fit different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she gets a proper גט, she is fully divorced, and a divorced woman never needs חליצה. So asking for both looks like an overlap. The question sets up the explanation that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (both things?!)

phrases.english: Two?!
phrases.notes: He means: once she gets a good גט, why would she ever need חליצה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the double requirement in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling requiring both a גט and חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A valid גט makes חליצה unnecessary, so requiring both seems contradictory.

steps.title: A גט while he lives, חליצה after he dies
steps.stepSummary: The two requirements apply at different times: a גט if the husband is alive, חליצה if he dies first.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גט while the husband is alive, and חליצה after his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two remedies are not needed together. Each one fits a different time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the husband is alive, he should give her a fresh, definite גט. If he dies before doing that, and she might need יבום, she does חליצה instead, since יבום is not allowed for a woman who may already be divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: While (the husband is) alive
After (the husband's) death

steps.whatToRemember: In a doubtful divorce we are strict both ways: a new גט while the husband is alive, or חליצה (never יבום) if he dies first.

phrases.english: A bill of divorce while he is alive,
and chalitza after his death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ruling into two different time periods
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought she needed both a גט and חליצה at once.
steps.terutzMaskana: She needs a גט if the husband is alive; if he dies without giving one, she needs חליצה.

steps.title: The misspelled name: the witnesses' job is over
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses wrote the wrong name in a גט, and רב rules they have already finished their mission and cannot write another.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a woman called נפאתה, and the witnesses went and wrote תפאתה. רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא said in the name of רב: the witnesses have finished their mission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case. The husband sent witnesses to write and give a גט, but they misspelled the wife's name, and רב rules that they cannot write a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט with the wrong name is not valid. רב's point is that the husband's appointment covered one writing, and the witnesses already used it up. To write a new גט, they would need a new appointment from the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses (Aramaic for עדים)
The witnesses have finished their mission
Being someone's agent, acting on his behalf

phrases.english: A certain woman whom they would call "Nefata",
the witnesses went and wrote "Tefata".
phrases.notes: The husband had told these witnesses to write the גט and give it to her, and they got her name wrong.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said in the name of Rav:
The witnesses have performed their mission.
phrases.notes: So that גט is no good, and they can't just write a corrected one on their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about when an agent's mission ends, connected to the theme of incomplete שליחות in steps 20-21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the witnesses have written the גט, even a flawed one, their mission is over, and they cannot write another.

steps.title: רבה: the husband did not ask for a worthless paper
steps.stepSummary: רבה argues that writing a useless גט cannot count as finishing the mission.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה challenged this: Did the husband tell them, "Write a broken piece of pottery and give it to her"?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב's ruling. The husband wanted a real גט, so writing a useless one did not do what he asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An agent's job is defined by what the sender asked for. The husband asked for a valid גט, not a worthless one. So a גט with the wrong name does not use up the mission.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (introduces an objection)
A broken piece of pottery, meaning something worthless

phrases.english: Rabba challenged it:
Did he say to them,
"Write a shard and give it to her"?!
phrases.notes: A גט with the wrong name is as useless as a broken piece of pottery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the witnesses finished their mission
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mission was to write a valid גט; an invalid one does not fulfill or end it.

steps.title: רבה: only a valid גט that was lost ends the mission
steps.stepSummary: רבה limits רב's rule to a case where the witnesses wrote a good גט and then lost it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: Certainly, if the witnesses wrote a proper גט and it got lost, then the witnesses have finished their mission.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב's case, רבה says when the rule really applies: a valid גט that was written and then lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, the mission is to write a valid גט. Once they did that, the job is done even if the paper later disappears. A misspelled גט never fulfilled the job, so the witnesses may still write a correct one.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly
A good, valid גט
And it got lost

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said: Certainly,
if the witnesses wrote a proper bill of divorce,
and it was lost,
the witnesses have performed their mission.
phrases.notes: So in that case they could not write another one, but in the misspelled case they could.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers רבה's own version of the rule after his challenge in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witnesses' mission ends once they write a valid גט, even if it is later lost; an invalid גט does not end it.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the husband did not ask them to keep it in their pockets
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן argues that the mission includes giving the גט, not just writing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged this: Did the husband tell them, "Write it and put it in your pockets"?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רבה's view. The husband wanted the גט written and given to his wife, not just written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה treated writing a valid גט as the end of the job. רב נחמן points out that the husband's request was to divorce her. Until the גט actually reaches the wife, the mission is not finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Put it down, keep it
Your pockets

phrases.english: Rav Nachman challenged it:
Did he say to them,
"Write it and put it in your pockets"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's rule in step 30, using the same style of argument רבה used against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that writing a valid גט that was later lost ends the mission
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mission was to write and give the גט; writing alone, without giving it, does not complete it.

steps.title: רב נחמן: write and give, even a hundred times
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the witnesses may keep writing and giving the גט until a valid one reaches the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: they write and give, even a hundred times.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives his own ruling. Since the job is only done when the wife receives a valid גט, the witnesses can try again as many times as needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion moved the finish line later. For רב, the job ends with writing. For רבה, it ends with writing a valid גט. For רב נחמן, it ends only with giving a valid גט to the wife, so a lost or flawed גט just means they write another.

keyTerms.meaning: They write and they give
A hundred times, meaning as many times as needed

steps.whatToRemember: Three steps on one question: when is the witnesses' mission over? רב says once they write; רבה says once they write a valid גט; רב נחמן says only once a valid גט is given to the wife.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said:
They write and give,
even a hundred times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב נחמן's own rule after his challenge in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witnesses' mission ends only when a valid גט is given to the wife; until then they may write and give it again, even a hundred times.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The witnesses' mission is defined by the husband's goal, which is to divorce his wife, so it is not finished until that actually happens.

steps.title: Does handing the גט to an agent end the witnesses' job?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן about a husband who said 'Write and give it to a שליח.' Did he end the witnesses' role once they hand it over, or was he only saving them effort?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: if the husband said 'Write a גט and give it to an agent,' what is the law? Did he take the witnesses off the job once they give it to the agent, or was he just trying to save them the trouble of delivering it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds on רב נחמן's ruling that witnesses may keep writing until a valid גט reaches the wife. He asks what happens when the husband told them to hand the גט to a שליח instead of bringing it themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read the husband's words. Maybe he meant that their job ends when they give the גט to the שליח, so they cannot write again. Or maybe he only wanted to spare them the trip, so their job stays open until a valid גט reaches her.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him (presents a question for a ruling)
Agent, messenger
He removed them (ended their job)
Effort, trouble

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
If the husband said 'Write, and give it to an agent,' what is the law?
Did he remove them from the job once they gave it over,
or perhaps he was only concerned about their effort?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב נחמן's ruling against a husband who sent the גט through an agent
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the instruction to give the גט to a שליח ends the witnesses' job or only spares them effort

steps.title: What if the husband added 'and he will bring it to her'?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי about the same instruction with the added words 'and he will bring it to her.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: if the husband said 'Write, give it to an agent, and he will bring it to her,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes רבא's question further. He asks what happens if the husband also said the שליח will bring the גט to the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'he will bring it to her' may show that the husband cares about the גט actually reaching the wife. If so, the witnesses' job would continue until that happens, and they could write again if needed. Or the extra words may change nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And he will bring it to her
What is the law?

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
If the husband added 'and he will bring it to her,' what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's question by adding more wording
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the words 'and he will bring it to her' keep the witnesses' job open until the גט reaches her

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the question unanswered with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand: the question is not resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this discussion without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source settled the question. We do not know whether the words 'and he will bring it to her' extend the witnesses' job.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The witnesses' mission (steps 28–35): רב said they finish once they write. רבה limited that to a good גט that was lost. רב נחמן said they may keep going until a valid גט reaches her. Whether the husband's instruction to hand the גט to a שליח changes this is left open.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבינא's question without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of 'and he will bring it to her' remains unresolved

steps.title: 'Take my גט for me' also makes a receiving agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the משנה: a woman who says 'טול לי גיטי' has made a receiving agent, so the husband cannot take the גט back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even when a woman says 'Take my גט for me,' if the husband wants to take it back, he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that 'take my גט for me' works the same way as 'receive my גט for me.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the גט reaches a שליח קבלה, the wife is divorced, so the husband can no longer change his mind. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds 'טול לי' to the phrases that create this kind of agent.

keyTerms.meaning: Take my גט for me
To retract, to take back
An agent who receives the גט for the wife

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even a woman who says 'Take my bill of divorce for me,'
if he wants to retract, he cannot retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next part of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'טול לי גיטי' makes a שליח קבלה, so the husband cannot retract once the agent has the גט

steps.title: A list of phrases that mean receiving
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists 'טול לי,' 'שא לי,' and 'יהא לי בידך' as phrases of receiving.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Take for me,' 'Lift for me,' and 'Let it be in your hand for me' are all phrases of receiving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that expands רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's point. It names several phrases that all appoint a receiving agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These phrases join 'טול לי' in counting as לשון קבלה. As soon as the agent gets the גט, the divorce takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Lift it for me
Let it be in your hand for me
Language of receiving

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Take for me,' and 'Lift for me,'
and 'Let it be in your hand for me' –
all of them are expressions of receiving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling with more phrases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'טול לי,' 'שא לי,' and 'יהא לי בידך' all appoint a שליח קבלה

steps.title: New משנה: two sets of witnesses for a receiving agent
steps.stepSummary: A woman who says 'התקבל לי גיטי' needs two sets of witnesses: one for the appointment and one for the agent receiving and tearing the גט. The same two people can serve as both sets.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who said 'Receive my גט for me' needs two sets of witnesses. Two say 'She said it in front of us,' and two say 'He received it and tore it in front of us.' This works even if the first pair and the second pair are the same people,
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains what testimony is needed to prove a woman was divorced through a שליח קבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate facts need proof. First, that she appointed the agent. Second, that the agent actually received the גט. The משנה adds that the same two witnesses can testify to both facts.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Receive my גט for me
Two sets of witnesses
In front of us, in our presence
He tore it

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A woman who said: 'Receive my bill of divorce for me,'
needs two sets of witnesses –
two who say: 'In our presence she said it,'
and two who say: 'In our presence he received it and tore it';
phrases.notes: 'He' is the agent: these witnesses saw him get the גט.

phrases.english: even if the same people are the first pair and the latter pair,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on the testimony needed for a שליח קבלה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A divorce through a שליח קבלה needs witnesses to both the appointment and the receiving. The same two people may testify to both.
